Base directory for this skill: /home/user/Claudinite/.claude/skills/verify-in-production

# Verify in production

A change is finished when someone has watched it work. Most changes you can watch **now**, and
that is the rule — this skill is only for the rest: a change whose proof lives somewhere the
repo cannot see yet. You are filing the proof, not doing the work — and the proof itself runs
unattended: an automatic check, end to end, with a person entering
only where no automatic check can exist.

## When it fires: after the merge, never before

**The PR must have merged.** This skill runs as a step of the merge, unasked — `merge-to-main`
calls it once the squash has landed — and at no other moment. Not when the code is written, not
when the PR opens, not while review is in flight.

The reason is that a PR can be **rejected**, and a branch that is still open can be rewritten
under you. Both leave a verification whose premise never reached `main`:

- A **rewritten branch** makes the brief describe a change that no longer exists. #1121 was filed
  against a scope its PR then dropped; the verification was moot before the merge it waited on.
- A **rejected PR** is worse, because the queue cannot tell it from a merge. A blocked item
  releases on its blocker being *closed*, and nothing reads `merged` — so the item goes ready,
  reads an `In-production-when:` that can never become true, pushes `Not-before:` forward by
  `Retry-every:` without comment, and repeats indefinitely. No janitor rule reclaims it: the
  stale-ready sweep cannot see an item sleeping on a future `Not-before`, and the
  stuck-dependency sweep exempts an item whose blockers have closed.

So there is no such thing as filing this early and letting the queue sort it out. Wait for the
merge, then read **what actually landed** — the merged diff, not the branch you remember writing.

## First: does this file anything at all?

Most changes **file nothing.** Run the test in this order and stop at the first answer:

1. **Did you watch it work in this session?** Then it is proven. File nothing.
2. **Did a test that ran prove it?** A unit test, a CI job, an executable-requirements or UI
   test covering exactly the behaviour that changed. File nothing — the suite is the mechanism
   that comes back.
3. **Does the change have an observable effect at all?** A comment, a design doc, a README, a
   rename with no behavioural edge, a refactor a passing suite already pins. File nothing.
4. **Otherwise: where does its effect first become observable?** If the answer is a place and a
   moment — a member repo once it converges, a site once it deploys, a session once it reloads
   its rules — that is what you file.

The bar is *could not be watched now*, not *would be nice to double-check*. A verification
filed for a change already covered by a test is a wasted run re-proving what the suite proved.

## What you file

**A deferred request** — the same ad-hoc lane `/do-later` rides, so the queue does the waiting,
the running and the lifecycle; nothing here adds machinery beside it. One issue, titled
`Verify in production: <the change, in a few words>`, its body the whole brief: the run that
verifies will never see this conversation and may be days away. Say what changed and why it
could not be watched now, then, each spelled verbatim on its own line:

```
Original-issue: #<the change's issue>
In-production-when: <the concrete artifact to read, and what makes it true>
Verify: <what to observe, and what counts as a pass>
Not-before: <ISO instant just past the expected release>
Retry-every: <how far to push Not-before when not yet live, e.g. 1 day>
```

No `Blocked-by:`. You are filing after the merge, so the change's PR has already closed and
there is nothing left to wait on but the release itself.

- **`Original-issue:`** is where a failure lands — the issue the change was done under, which
  the run reopens if the verification fails. Make the verification that issue's **sub-issue**
  too (`mcp__github__sub_issue_write`, method `add`, `issue_number` the original,
  `sub_issue_id` the **id** the create call returned, not its number), so the change it proves
  shows what is still unproven about it — [RULES.md](../../RULES.md)' *Filing an issue that
  belongs under another*, applied where there is no PR left to carry the link.
- **`In-production-when:`** names a thing to *read*, never a duration to wait. "`missingbulb/Shepherd`'s
  `.claudinite-checks.json` stamps `packVersions.tidy-repo` at 8 or higher." "The live site's
  `/version.json` reports a version past 4.2.0." "Any session started after this landed — check
  the vendored copy under `.claudinite/shared/` carries the new text." A merge is not a
  production condition, and neither is elapsed time.
- **`Verify:`** is an assertion with a pass condition, not a topic — and a read an **unattended
  run can make**: an API response, a file at a URL, an issue's state. "Issue #100 on that repo
  is closed with a comment citing the scheduler runs" beats "check tidy-issues works". Only where no
  automatic check can exist may `Verify:` name a person's step, spelled out exactly.
- **`Not-before:`** is the queue's own wait field: adoption holds the run until the moment has
  passed. Aim it just past the release you expect — the re-arm covers a miss, so don't pad it.
- **`Retry-every:`** is the extension you are prescribing: when the run finds the change not
  yet live, it pushes `Not-before:` forward by exactly this much. Size it to the release you
  wait on — a nightly converge retries daily, a next-session rule in minutes.

Then the mark, as `/do-later` applies it: **`task:origin:ad-hoc`**, the one label the scheduler
run adopts. Beside it, in the body, **`Model: sonnet`** (reading a live artifact and judging an
assertion against it). Never `Automerge:` — a verification has nothing to merge. If the mark
doesn't exist in the repo yet, say so and leave the issue — it appears on the next scheduler run.

## Tell the run how to converge

End the body with instructions to the run itself — the issue is its whole brief, and the run
decides nothing: it executes this playbook.

1. Read `In-production-when:` against the real artifact. Never infer it from a merge, a green
   run, or elapsed time.
2. **Live** → run `Verify:`. Passes: comment the evidence actually read (the version, the value,
   the URL) and close this issue as completed. Fails: reopen `Original-issue:` with a comment
   saying what was asserted, what happened instead and where you read it; comment here linking
   that; close this issue as completed — the verification did its job by finding the fault.
3. **Not yet live** → push `Not-before:` forward by `Retry-every:`, **clear the issue's
   `task:status:*` label** (clearing the status is the whole of the re-ask — the mark stays on
   for life), and leave the issue open. The next scheduler run re-adopts it, and the bumped
   field holds it until the new moment. No comment; the bumped field is the record.

## Then say what you filed

One line back to the owner: the issue link, what it waits on, and its retry cadence.

input.command:
git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Collapse the frequency vocabulary, with one normalization door at the load point

`hourly` cannot mean anything under a cron that fires twice a day, and the
`daily±Nh` offsets staggered dependent tasks by clock hour where `after:`
declares the same intent and actually enforces it. FREQUENCIES becomes
daily/weekly/monthly/manual.

THE DOOR IS AT DECLARATION LOAD, in normalizeTaskDeclaration — not in the
calendar. A frequency is read by more than the anchor: periodMs feeds the
janitor's stale-ready bound and the precondition's signal window, so
normalizing only anchorInstant would judge a task that now runs daily stale
after two HOURS, parking it needs-human on exactly the members the tolerance
exists for. The tolerance is permanent, not a window: a task declaration is
member-owned data no vendoring pass rewrites. The author-time
declaration-shape check is what stops a NEW declaration naming a retired
token.

Four declarations move. `update` daily-2h -> daily (the chain head).
`growth-extract` daily-1h -> daily, already carrying the `after:` that ordered
it. `fleet-digest` daily+1h -> daily plus `after:` naming the three sheepdog
sweeps — inert where that pack is not declared, and unlike the offset it holds
when a sweep runs long. `usage-fold` hourly -> daily, and its WINDOW_DAYS with
it: sized to an hour while the task anchors daily, the "session captured" arm
never fires again and a repo whose only movement is commit-less sessions
silently stops folding.

The cross-repo half `after:` cannot express — members extract, then this repo's
growth-promote reads what merged on their mains — moves to this repo's own
dailyHour, now 5 against members' default 4. growth-promote also declares
`after:` for the within-repo half.

The simulator models the door too, and the scenarios that asserted the old
vocabulary move with it: S1', S22, S28, S34, S65, S67 re-derived, and S70
becomes the door's own scenario. S34 now settles a whole morning in one drain
and S65's day costs 28 invocations instead of 29 — the collapse paying for
itself in scenarios that predate it. S67's slip against the hourly grid is now
zero: the 22 extra runs bought latency for ad-hoc work and nothing for the
schedule. `monthly` is modeled rather than throwing.

Refs #1225
EOF

input.body:
Phases B and C of #1225, together — they have to land in the same cycle, because a member that received the collapsed vocabulary without the new cron would keep paying for 24 ticks, and one that received the cron without the vocabulary would see its `daily±Nh` tasks fire at hours no tick lands on.

Design: `docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` §17, merged in #1226.

## The vocabulary

`FREQUENCIES` becomes `daily`/`weekly`/`monthly`/`manual`. `hourly` cannot mean anything under a cron that fires twice a day, and the `daily±Nh` offsets staggered dependent tasks by clock hour where `after:` declares the same intent and actually enforces it.

**The door is at declaration load** (`normalizeTaskDeclaration`), not in the calendar. This is the finding that shaped the change: a frequency is read by more than the anchor — `periodMs` feeds the janitor's stale-ready bound and the precondition's signal window — so normalizing only `anchorInstant` would judge a task that now runs daily **stale after two hours**, parking it `needs-human` on exactly the members the tolerance exists to protect. The tolerance is permanent, not a migration window: a task declaration is member-owned data that no vendoring pass rewrites.

Four declarations move. `usage-fold`'s is the one with a trap — its `WINDOW_DAYS` was sized to its hourly period, and left there the "session captured" arm never fires again, so a repo whose only movement is commit-less sessions silently stops folding.

The cross-repo ordering `after:` **cannot** express — members extract, then this repo's `growth-promote` reads what merged on their mains — moves to this repo's own `dailyHour`, now 5 against members' default 4.

## What the simulator says

The collapse pays for itself in scenarios that predate it: S34 now settles a whole morning in one drain, and S65's working day costs 28 invocations instead of 29. **S67's slip against the hourly grid is now zero** — the 22 extra runs an hourly cron bills were buying latency for ad-hoc work and nothing at all for the schedule.

S70 becomes the door's own scenario; `monthly` is modeled rather than throwing.

## See-it-fail

- Removing the door from `normalizeTaskDeclaration` → 2 engine tests red.
- Removing the author-time strictness → the retired-spellings test red.
- Removing the `cronHours` filter → all seven cadence scenarios red.

Suite 2598/2598. `check_the_work` clean, `check_the_world` 0 blocking — one barriers finding was fixed rather than waived, by deleting the pack path from an engine comment.

Closes #1228

input.title: Collapse the frequency vocabulary and take the cron to two ticks a day
input.body:
Phases B and C of #1225, landing together — a member with the collapsed vocabulary but the old cron keeps paying for 24 ticks, and one with the new cron but the old vocabulary fires `daily±Nh` tasks at hours no tick lands on.

**B — the vocabulary.** `FREQUENCIES` becomes `daily`/`weekly`/`monthly`/`manual`, with the retired tokens accepted permanently and normalized at one door in `normalizeTaskDeclaration` — not in the calendar, because `periodMs` also feeds the janitor's stale bound and the signal window. Four declarations move (`update`, `growth-extract`, `fleet-digest`, `usage-fold` + its `WINDOW_DAYS`); the cross-repo stagger moves to this repo's `dailyHour: 5`.

**C — the cron.** `hashedCron` returns `<minute> <dailyHour>,<(dailyHour+12)%24>`; the converge passes the repo's schedule; the vendored stub and the canon's own workflow copy change in the same commit.

Closed by #1230. Delivery to the fleet, its verification, and the retirement of the door tolerance are the execution chain under #1225.

{"id":5221773732,"number":1225,"state":"open","locked":false,"title":"The hourly scheduler cron is the fleet's whole Actions allowance — move to a twice-daily tick","body":"## The problem

The August usage report puts `claudinite-scheduler.yml` at 1,515 of 2,123 private Actions minutes — **71% of spend** — running at a near-identical ~26 min/day on every private member (MissingBulbWebsite 26.1, WIP 27.0, hitbut 26.0, ClaudiniteWebsite 25.2, EdFringeAllocator 17.0).

Four private members × 24 min/day × 30d = 2,880 min = **$17.28/mo**, which is exactly the $18.00 allowance the report terminates at. The scheduler *is* the allowance, with zero macOS and zero real work. It scales linearly with adoption: WIP and hitbut came online Aug 20–21 and immediately added ~53 min/day between them.

## Why optimising the job buys nothing

Sampled 30 consecutive scheduled runs on this repo: **median 32s wall-clock**, only one over 60s. Actions bills each job rounded up to the whole minute, so ~46% of every billed minute is already rounding waste.

The cost is **run count**, not compute. The only lever is fewer runs.

## What the 24 runs/day are actually buying

Exactly one task in the corpus is `hourly` — `usage-fold` (`packs/claudinite-growth`). Everything else is `daily-2h`/`daily-1h`/`daily`/`daily+1h`/`weekly`/`monthly`/`manual`. Per `engine/scheduler/calendar.mjs`, the whole daily family lands at `dailyHour-2 … dailyHour+1`, with weekly and monthly also at `dailyHour` — so a default member's entire anchor set is four clock hours a day.

Two of the three remaining jobs are already solved elsewhere in the engine:

- **Ordering within a repo.** `after:` shipped (`engine/scheduler/task-contract.mjs:184-192`); `growth-extract` declares it and its own comment says the staggered hours *"express the same intent and cannot enforce it; this can."*
- **Chain continuation.** `executor.mjs:215` re-reads the queue each iteration and calls `readyDependents()` on every close, so a multi-stage chain drains back-to-back in one run.

That leaves adopting newly-marked ad-hoc issues, `Not-before` releases, and dead-claim reclaims as the only work the 23 extra runs a day exist for.

## The end state

`docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` §17, with the measured trade and the rejected alternatives. Cron fires twice daily at `<hashed-minute> <dailyHour>,<(dailyHour+12)%24>`. **24 runs/day → 2**; $17.28/mo → $1.44/mo; a new private member costs 2 min/day instead of 26.

---

# The plan

## Phase 0 — out-of-band setup: **none**

Verified there is no human-only step. No new secret, permission, repo variable or platform setting. The one path a converge cannot push into is `.github/workflows/`, and that is already solved: `pendingSchedulerWorkflow` (`updates/pack-update.mjs:161`) computes the target and **withholds** it, and the `update` task's apply stage lands it through the member's own PR lane. The cron rewrite reaches every member on the existing nightly cycle with nobody in the loop.

## Phase 1 — the approved stack (one review pass)

All code written before approval is asked for, including the destructive tail.

- [ ] **PR A — #1226 (open).** Design + simulator: `cronHours`, S67–S73, DESIGN §17, coverage rows. Closes #1227.
      *Exit:* merged.
- [ ] **PR B — the vocabulary.** Split `FREQUENCIES` (what a NEW declaration may name) from an accept-at-the-door set, with **one normalization door at declaration load** — not inside `anchorInstant`, because `periodMs` also feeds the janitor's stale-ready bound (`queue/janitor-rules.mjs:103`) and the signal window (`queue/signals.mjs:15`); normalizing only the anchor judges a daily task stale after two hours. Four consumers: `calendar.mjs:25`, `task-contract.mjs:100`, `packs/claudinite-growth/task-declaration-shape.mjs:49` (rejects the retired tokens for new declarations), `slots.mjs:23` (fielded shim, stays).
      Four declarations move: `update` `daily-2h`→`daily`; `growth-extract` `daily-1h`→`daily` (already has `after:`); `fleet-digest` `daily+1h`→`daily` + a new `after:` naming the sheepdog sweeps (safe cross-pack — an undeclared upstream yields no constraint); `usage-fold` `hourly`→`daily` **and its `WINDOW_DAYS = 2/24` must move with it**, or the "session captured" half of its precondition goes permanently dark and a repo whose only movement is commit-less sessions never folds again.
      Plus the cross-repo stagger `after:` cannot express: **set this repo's `taskScheduler.dailyHour` to 5**, so members extract at 04:00 and the canon's `growth-promote` reads their merged mains at 05:00. One line, this repo only, no fleet migration. Add `after: ['claudinite-growth/growth-extract']` to the canon-local `growth-promote` for the within-repo half.
      *Exit:* merged, suite green, S74 (normalized `hourly` behaves as `daily`) added and passing.
- [ ] **PR C — the cron.** `hashedCron` returns two hours derived from `dailyHour`; `converge-wiring.mjs:132` passes the schedule; the vendored stub's placeholder and **the canon's own `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml` change in the same commit** — the canon has no converge, so its copy drifts invisibly otherwise.
      *Exit:* merged; this repo's own workflow reads the two-hour cron.
- [ ] **PR D — the destructive tail, written now, merged later.** Retire the door-normalization and drop the legacy tokens from the accepted set. Body states its merge is gated on Link 3 and names it.
      *Exit:* approved in this pass; **not merged**.

## Phase 2 — the execution chain

Filed as sub-issues of this tracker once the plan is agreed, each naming the previous in `Blocked-by:` so the queue does the waiting.

- [ ] **Link 1 — force delivery and read it back.** Drive Shepherd's `fleet-baseline` with `follow`.
      *Ready when:* PRs B and C are merged.
      *Worked when:* every member's stamp shows the new `packVersions`, **and** its `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml` cron reads `<hashed> H,H+12` for that member's own `dailyHour`. Read per member; a member that cannot be read parks the link open rather than passing — a scope-blocked sweep answers "all clear" exactly like a healthy one.
- [ ] **Link 2 — verify in production.** *Ready when:* Link 1 closed and one full UTC day has passed.
      *Worked when:* each private member's Actions usage shows exactly **2** scheduler runs for that day (baseline: 24), and no task's standing item is missing its occurrence. Also the first read of the risk the sim cannot model — whether a member's whole daily chain now fits one drain against `timeout-minutes: 350`.
- [ ] **Link 3 — retire the tolerance.** *Ready when:* Link 2 closed **and** no member's task declarations still name a retired token — a converge-confirmable precondition, never a calendar date: retiring it while a member still declares `hourly` turns that member's daily task into a two-hour staleness park.
      *Worked when:* PR D merged, suite green.

## Known residual risks

- **Dropped ticks cost 12× more latency** (S71). Nothing is stranded — dueness comes from the anchor, never from whether the cron fired — but a dropped anchor tick now waits until the drain tick. This is why the second tick is not optional.
- **Ad-hoc latency goes to a 6h mean / 12h worst case** (S68). An `issues: [labeled]` trigger would take it to seconds for a run only when a mark happens; recorded in §17.5 as additive and deliberately out of this plan's scope.
- **A whole day now settles serially in one Actions job.** The simulator's durations are fixtures, so it cannot say whether a real member's chain fits. Link 2 is the first real measurement.

Also the first read of the risk the sim cannot model — whether a member's whole daily chain now fits one drain against `timeout-minutes: 350`.
- [ ] **Link 3 — retire the tolerance.** *Ready when:* Link 2 closed **and** no member's task declarations still name a retired token — a converge-confirmable precondition, never a calendar date: retiring it while a member still declares `hourly` turns that member's daily task into a two-hour staleness park.

## Known residual risks

- **Dropped ticks cost 12× more latency** (S71). Nothing is stranded — dueness comes from the anchor, never from whether the cron fired — but a dropped anchor tick now waits until the drain tick. This is why the second tick is not optional.
- **Ad-hoc latency goes to a 6h mean / 12h worst case** (S68). An `issues: [labeled]` trigger would take it to seconds for a run only when a mark happens; recorded in §17.5 as additive and deliberately out of this plan's scope.
- **A whole day now settles serially in one Actions job.** The simulator's durations are fixtures, so it cannot say whether a real member's chain fits. Link 2 is the first real measurement.

Phases B and C of #1225, together — they have to land in the same cycle. A member with the collapsed vocabulary but the old cron keeps paying for 24 ticks; one with the new cron but the old vocabulary fires its `daily±Nh` tasks at hours no tick lands on.

Design: `docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` §17, merged in #1226.

## B — the vocabulary

`FREQUENCIES` becomes `daily`/`weekly`/`monthly`/`manual`. `hourly` cannot mean anything under a cron that fires twice a day, and the `daily±Nh` offsets staggered dependent tasks by clock hour where `after:` declares the same intent and actually enforces it.

**The door is at declaration load** (`normalizeTaskDeclaration`), not in the calendar. This is the finding that shaped the change: a frequency is read by more than the anchor — `periodMs` feeds the janitor's stale-ready bound and the precondition's signal window — so normalizing only `anchorInstant` would judge a task that now runs daily **stale after two hours**, parking it `needs-human` on exactly the members the tolerance exists to protect. The tolerance is permanent: a task declaration is member-owned data no vendoring pass rewrites.

Four declarations move. `usage-fold`'s carries the trap — its `WINDOW_DAYS` was sized to its hourly period, and left there the "session captured" arm never fires again, so a repo whose only movement is commit-less sessions silently stops folding.

The cross-repo ordering `after:` **cannot** express — members extract, then this repo's `growth-promote` reads what merged on their mains — moves to this repo's own `dailyHour`, now 5 against members' default 4.

## C — the cron

`hashedCron` returns `<minute> <dailyHour>,<(dailyHour+12)%24> * * *`, threaded through `convergeWiring`, the pack-update lane and bootstrap. Pinning the hours to a constant would fire every task before its anchor on any member that moved its schedule — a day late forever, with nothing going red — so the rehearsal gains a `custom-anchor-hour` shape and `converge-wiring` asserts the hours that actually land.

`scheduler-workflow-shape` accepts both cron forms: `.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot push, so a member holds its hourly cron until its apply-stage PR lands, and going red in that window would fire the check on every member the change hasn't reached yet.

The canon's own workflow copy moves in the same commit — hand-maintained, no converge, drifts invisibly otherwise.

## Consumer safety

Chose the **fixture**, not a migration record: nothing here renames or requires anything of a member's own files. `custom-anchor-hour` is the honest new shape — a member on a non-default `dailyHour` still holding the hourly cron.

## What the simulator says

The collapse pays for itself in scenarios that predate it: S34 now settles a whole morning in one drain, S65's working day costs 28 invocations instead of 29. **S67's slip against the hourly grid is now zero** — the 22 extra runs an hourly cron bills were buying latency for ad-hoc work and nothing at all for the schedule. S70 becomes the door's own scenario; `monthly` is modeled rather than throwing.

## See-it-fail

Each guard was driven red and back: removing the door (2 engine tests), removing the author-time strictness, drifting the duplicated default hour, drifting the canon's cron from the computed value, making the converge ignore `dailyHour`, and removing the `cronHours` filter (all seven cadence scenarios).

Suite 2606/2606. `check_the_work` and `check_the_world` both 0 blocking — two findings were fixed rather than waived (a barriers crossing in an engine comment, an over-long `fix` string).

Closes #1231

input.body:
**This PR is written for review now and merged later.** Phase D of #1225 — the destructive tail. `writing-migration-plans`: all the code including the tail is written and approved in one pass so the owner's attention is spent once; what waits is the *merge*, and what performs it is a link in the chain rather than anyone's memory.

Stacked on #1230 (phases B and C). Base moves to `main` once that lands.

## What it removes, and what gates each

**The frequency tolerance.** `LEGACY_FREQUENCIES` is **emptied, not deleted** — the map *is* the tolerance, so emptying it collapses `ACCEPTED_FREQUENCIES` onto `FREQUENCIES`, makes a declaration still naming a retired token fail contract validation, and leaves `normalizeFrequency` as the identity every caller can keep calling. Nothing has to be unwired, and a later retirement fills the map in again.

> *Gate:* no member's own task declarations still name a retired token. Converge-confirmable, never a date. Emptying early doesn't merely fail such a task — it makes `periodMs` judge it against a bound it was never sized for, which is the two-hour staleness park the whole door exists to prevent.

{"id":5221773732,"number":1225,"state":"open","locked":false,"title":"The hourly scheduler cron is the fleet's whole Actions allowance — move to a twice-daily tick","body":"## The problem

The August usage report puts `claudinite-scheduler.yml` at 1,515 of 2,123 private Actions minutes — **71% of spend** — running at a near-identical ~26 min/day on every private member (MissingBulbWebsite 26.1, WIP 27.0, hitbut 26.0, ClaudiniteWebsite 25.2, EdFringeAllocator 17.0).

Four private members × 24 min/day × 30d = 2,880 min = **$17.28/mo**, which is exactly the $18.00 allowance the report terminates at. The scheduler *is* the allowance, with zero macOS and zero real work. It scales linearly with adoption: WIP and hitbut came online Aug 20–21 and immediately added ~53 min/day between them.

## Why optimising the job buys nothing

Sampled 30 consecutive scheduled runs on this repo: **median 32s wall-clock**, only one over 60s. Actions bills each job rounded up to the whole minute, so ~46% of every billed minute is already rounding waste.

The cost is **run count**, not compute. The only lever is fewer runs.

## What the 24 runs/day are actually buying

Exactly one task in the corpus is `hourly` — `usage-fold` (`packs/claudinite-growth`). Everything else is `daily-2h`/`daily-1h`/`daily`/`daily+1h`/`weekly`/`monthly`/`manual`. Per `engine/scheduler/calendar.mjs`, the whole daily family lands at `dailyHour-2 … dailyHour+1`, with weekly and monthly also at `dailyHour` — so a default member's entire anchor set is four clock hours a day.

Two of the three remaining jobs are already solved elsewhere in the engine:

- **Ordering within a repo.** `after:` shipped (`engine/scheduler/task-contract.mjs:184-192`); `growth-extract` declares it and its own comment says the staggered hours *"express the same intent and cannot enforce it; this can."*
- **Chain continuation.** `executor.mjs:215` re-reads the queue each iteration and calls `readyDependents()` on every close, so a multi-stage chain drains back-to-back in one run.

That leaves adopting newly-marked ad-hoc issues, `Not-before` releases, and dead-claim reclaims as the only work the 23 extra runs a day exist for.

## The end state

`docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` §17, with the measured trade and the rejected alternatives. Cron fires twice daily at `<hashed-minute> <dailyHour>,<(dailyHour+12)%24>`. **24 runs/day → 2**; $17.28/mo → $1.44/mo; a new private member costs 2 min/day instead of 26.

---

# The plan

## Phase 0 — out-of-band setup: **none**

Verified there is no human-only step. No new secret, permission, repo variable or platform setting. The one path a converge cannot push into is `.github/workflows/`, and that is already solved: `pendingSchedulerWorkflow` (`updates/pack-update.mjs:161`) computes the target and **withholds** it, and the `update` task's apply stage lands it through the member's own PR lane. The cron rewrite reaches every member on the existing nightly cycle with nobody in the loop.

## Phase 1 — the approved stack (one review pass)

All code written before approval is asked for, including the destructive tail.

- [ ] **PR A — #1226 (open).** Design + simulator: `cronHours`, S67–S73, DESIGN §17, coverage rows. Closes #1227.
      *Exit:* merged.
- [ ] **PR B — the vocabulary.** Split `FREQUENCIES` (what a NEW declaration may name) from an accept-at-the-door set, with **one normalization door at declaration load** — not inside `anchorInstant`, because `periodMs` also feeds the janitor's stale-ready bound (`queue/janitor-rules.mjs:103`) and the signal window (`queue/signals.mjs:15`); normalizing only the anchor judges a daily task stale after two hours. Four consumers: `calendar.mjs:25`, `task-contract.mjs:100`, `packs/claudinite-growth/task-declaration-shape.mjs:49` (rejects the retired tokens for new declarations), `slots.mjs:23` (fielded shim, stays).
      Four declarations move: `update` `daily-2h`→`daily`; `growth-extract` `daily-1h`→`daily` (already has `after:`); `fleet-digest` `daily+1h`→`daily` + a new `after:` naming the sheepdog sweeps (safe cross-pack — an undeclared upstream yields no constraint); `usage-fold` `hourly`→`daily` **and its `WINDOW_DAYS = 2/24` must move with it**, or the "session captured" half of its precondition goes permanently dark and a repo whose only movement is commit-less sessions never folds again.
      Plus the cross-repo stagger `after:` cannot express: **set this repo's `taskScheduler.dailyHour` to 5**, so members extract at 04:00 and the canon's `growth-promote` reads their merged mains at 05:00. One line, this repo only, no fleet migration. Add `after: ['claudinite-growth/growth-extract']` to the canon-local `growth-promote` for the within-repo half.
      *Exit:* merged, suite green, S74 (normalized `hourly` behaves as `daily`) added and passing.
- [ ] **PR C — the cron.** `hashedCron` returns two hours derived from `dailyHour`; `converge-wiring.mjs:132` passes the schedule; the vendored stub's placeholder and **the canon's own `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml` change in the same commit** — the canon has no converge, so its copy drifts invisibly otherwise.
      *Exit:* merged; this repo's own workflow reads the two-hour cron.
- [ ] **PR D — the destructive tail, written now, merged later.** Retire the door-normalization and drop the legacy tokens from the accepted set. Body states its merge is gated on Link 3 and names it.
      *Exit:* approved in this pass; **not merged**.

## Phase 2 — the execution chain

Filed as sub-issues of this tracker once the plan is agreed, each naming the previous in `Blocked-by:` so the queue does the waiting.

- [ ] **Link 1 — force delivery and read it back.** Drive Shepherd's `fleet-baseline` with `follow`.
      *Ready when:* PRs B and C are merged.
      *Worked when:* every member's stamp shows the new `packVersions`, **and** its `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml` cron reads `<hashed> H,H+12` for that member's own `dailyHour`. Read per member; a member that cannot be read parks the link open rather than passing — a scope-blocked sweep answers "all clear" exactly like a healthy one.
- [ ] **Link 2 — verify in production.** *Ready when:* Link 1 closed and one full UTC day has passed.
      *Worked when:* each private member's Actions usage shows exactly **2** scheduler runs for that day (baseline: 24), and no task's standing item is missing its occurrence. Also the first read of the risk the sim cannot model — whether a member's whole daily chain now fits one drain against `timeout-minutes: 350`.
- [ ] **Link 3 — retire the tolerance.** *Ready when:* Link 2 closed **and** no member's task declarations still name a retired token — a converge-confirmable precondition, never a calendar date: retiring it while a member still declares `hourly` turns that member's daily task into a two-hour staleness park.
      *Worked when:* PR D merged, suite green.

## Known residual risks

- **Dropped ticks cost 12× more latency** (S71). Nothing is stranded — dueness comes from the anchor, never from whether the cron fired — but a dropped anchor tick now waits until the drain tick. This is why the second tick is not optional.
- **Ad-hoc latency goes to a 6h mean / 12h worst case** (S68). An `issues: [labeled]` trigger would take it to seconds for a run only when a mark happens; recorded in §17.5 as additive and deliberately out of this plan's scope.
- **A whole day now settles serially in one Actions job.** The simulator's durations are fixtures, so it cannot say whether a real member's chain fits. Link 2 is the first real measurement.

input.title: Chain 1/3: force the twice-daily cron onto every member, and read it back
input.body:
Link 1 of #1225's execution chain. You will never see the conversation that planned this — everything you need is here.

```
Blocked-by: #1231
Model: sonnet
```

## What changed, and why this needs forcing

The scheduler cron went from hourly to twice daily (`docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` §17): `<hashed-minute> <dailyHour>,<(dailyHour+12)%24> * * *`. That is a change to a contract members' own files must satisfy — a workflow file plus a frequency vocabulary — so the nightly converge is not enough on its own to answer *"did it work on every repo?"*.

## What makes this step's world ready

#1231 closed, meaning #1230 merged. The queue holds this until then.

## The playbook

1. Drive Shepherd's `fleet-baseline` with `follow`, so it converges every member and reports per member rather than dispatching and returning.
2. For **each** member, read two things from the member's own repo:
   - its stamp's `packVersions` — `claudinite-lifecycle` ≥ `60822.2`, `claudinite-growth` ≥ `60822.1`, `claudinite-dashboard` ≥ `60822.2`;
   - its `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml` `cron:` line.
3. The cron is member-specific. Compute the expected value rather than matching a constant: `node engine/scheduler/hash-minute.mjs <owner/repo>` for the minute, and the member's own `taskScheduler.dailyHour` (default 4) for the hours — so a default member expects `<minute> 4,16 * * *`.

## What counts as this step having worked

Every member reads back **both** the stamped pack versions and its own correct two-tick cron.

The workflow file is the half that can lag: `.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot push, so it lands through the member's `update` task apply-stage PR. A member whose stamp has moved but whose workflow PR is still open has **not** passed — note it and keep this issue open; it will pass on a later run once that PR lands.

## When the check fails

Comment what you actually read, per member, and **leave this issue open**. Closing is what releases the next link, so a failed step must not close.

A member you cannot read is a failure, not a pass. A scope-blocked or rate-limited sweep answers "all clear" in exactly the way a healthy fleet does — if a read did not succeed, say so rather than counting it.

## How it ends

Comment the per-member evidence on #1225, then close this issue as completed. That close releases Link 2.

input.title: Chain 2/3: verify the twice-daily cron in production — 2 scheduler runs a day, not 24
input.body:
Link 2 of #1225's execution chain. Everything you need is here.

```
Blocked-by: #1235
Not-before: 2026-08-25T06:00:00Z
Retry-every: 1 day
Model: sonnet
```

## What this proves

The whole point of the change: the scheduler was **71% of private Actions spend** at ~26 min/day per member, because Actions bills each job rounded up and the cron fired 24 times a day to do about 13 minutes of work. Two ticks a day should make that ~2 min/day. Nothing so far has measured a real repo — only the simulator.

## What makes this step's world ready

#1235 closed (every member on the new cron), **and** at least one full UTC day has elapsed since, so there is a complete day to count.

## What to observe

For each **private** member — the ones that cost anything; public repos are free and unlimited:

1. **The count.** Scheduler workflow runs for one complete UTC day. Expect exactly **2**. Baseline: 24.
2. **Nothing was dropped.** No task's standing item is missing its occurrence for that day — a cheaper cron that quietly stopped instantiating work is a regression, not a saving.
3. **The risk the simulator could not model.** A whole day's chain now settles serially inside one executor run. Read the longest executor run's duration against the workflow's `timeout-minutes: 350`. The simulator's task durations are fixtures, so this is the first real read of whether a member's day actually fits.

## What counts as this step having worked

Every private member shows 2 scheduler runs for the measured day, no missing occurrences, and no executor run near its timeout.

## When the check fails

Comment what you read and **leave this issue open** — closing releases the next link.

- Still 24 runs on some member → its workflow never landed; reopen #1235's question there rather than proceeding.
- Missing occurrences → this is a real regression in the cadence change. Reopen #1225 with what is missing and stop the chain.
- An executor run near the timeout → do **not** fail the step, but say so plainly on #1225: it is the residual risk the plan named, and it wants its own issue rather than silence.

## How it ends

Comment the per-member figures on #1225 — runs/day before and after, and the longest executor run — then close this issue as completed. That close releases Link 3.

input.title: Chain 3/3: retire the twice-daily-cron migration tolerances
input.body:
Link 3 of #1225's execution chain — the last one. Everything you need is here.

```
Blocked-by: #1236
Retry-every: 7 days
Model: sonnet
```

## What this removes

#1234 is written, reviewed and waiting. It empties `LEGACY_FREQUENCIES`, so `hourly` / `daily-2h` / `daily-1h` / `daily+1h` stop being accepted in a task declaration, and it stops `scheduler-workflow-shape` accepting the legacy hourly cron.

## What makes this step's world ready

#1236 closed, **and** the precondition below reads true. It is converge-confirmable, never a date — if it does not hold yet, this is a wait, not a failure.

**No member's own task declarations still name a retired frequency.** Canon packs are already migrated; what matters is each member's `.claudinite/local/packs/*/tasks/*/task.mjs`, which is member-authored and which no vendoring pass rewrites. Grep each member for `frequency: 'hourly'`, `'daily-2h'`, `'daily-1h'`, `'daily+1h'`.

Retiring early does not merely fail such a task. `periodMs` also feeds the janitor's stale-ready bound and the precondition's signal window, so an un-normalized token makes a daily task judged against a bound it was never sized for — a `needs-human` park on every sweep, on exactly the members the tolerance exists to protect.

## The playbook

1. Check the precondition across every member. If any still declares a retired token: comment which member and which file on #1225, push `Not-before` forward by `Retry-every`, clear this issue's `task:status:*` label, and leave it open. No other comment — the bumped field is the record. Fixing that member's declaration is the way to unblock this, and is worth doing.
2. Precondition holds → rebase #1234 onto current `main` and **re-run `check_the_work`**. Its `pack-version-bumped` result was a known false green while it was stacked on #1230 (#1119): the diff carried the lower PR's bump. Re-bump `claudinite-lifecycle` if the check now asks.
3. Run the full suite: `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`.
4. Green → merge #1234.

Note the two tolerances have **different** gates. The cron half's gate — every member's workflow PR landed — was already satisfied by #1235. If the frequency half is still blocked long after, the commit can be split and the cron half merged alone.

## What counts as this step having worked

#1234 merged, suite green, and no member red on its next converge.

## How it ends

Comment on #1225 that the tolerances are retired and the migration is complete, then close this issue as completed. #1225 can close with it.

{"id":5221773732,"number":1225,"state":"open","locked":false,"title":"The hourly scheduler cron is the fleet's whole Actions allowance — move to a twice-daily tick","body":"## The problem

The August usage report puts `claudinite-scheduler.yml` at 1,515 of 2,123 private Actions minutes — **71% of spend** — running at a near-identical ~26 min/day on every private member (MissingBulbWebsite 26.1, WIP 27.0, hitbut 26.0, ClaudiniteWebsite 25.2, EdFringeAllocator 17.0).

Four private members × 24 min/day × 30d = 2,880 min = **$17.28/mo**, which is exactly the $18.00 allowance the report terminates at. The scheduler *is* the allowance, with zero macOS and zero real work. It scales linearly with adoption: WIP and hitbut came online Aug 20–21 and immediately added ~53 min/day between them.

## Why optimising the job buys nothing

Sampled 30 consecutive scheduled runs on this repo: **median 32s wall-clock**, only one over 60s. Actions bills each job rounded up to the whole minute, so ~46% of every billed minute is already rounding waste.

The cost is **run count**, not compute. The only lever is fewer runs.

## What the 24 runs/day are actually buying

Exactly one task in the corpus is `hourly` — `usage-fold` (`packs/claudinite-growth`). Everything else is `daily-2h`/`daily-1h`/`daily`/`daily+1h`/`weekly`/`monthly`/`manual`. Per `engine/scheduler/calendar.mjs`, the whole daily family lands at `dailyHour-2 … dailyHour+1`, with weekly and monthly also at `dailyHour` — so a default member's entire anchor set is four clock hours a day.

Two of the three remaining jobs are already solved elsewhere in the engine:

- **Ordering within a repo.** `after:` shipped (`engine/scheduler/task-contract.mjs:184-192`); `growth-extract` declares it and its own comment says the staggered hours *"express the same intent and cannot enforce it; this can."*
- **Chain continuation.** `executor.mjs:215` re-reads the queue each iteration and calls `readyDependents()` on every close, so a multi-stage chain drains back-to-back in one run.

That leaves adopting newly-marked ad-hoc issues, `Not-before` releases, and dead-claim reclaims as the only work the 23 extra runs a day exist for.

## The end state

`docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` §17, with the measured trade and the rejected alternatives. Cron fires twice daily at `<hashed-minute> <dailyHour>,<(dailyHour+12)%24>`. **24 runs/day → 2**; $17.28/mo → $1.44/mo; a new private member costs 2 min/day instead of 26.

---

# The plan

## Phase 0 — out-of-band setup: **none**

Verified there is no human-only step. No new secret, permission, repo variable or platform setting. The one path a converge cannot push into is `.github/workflows/`, and that is already solved: `pendingSchedulerWorkflow` (`updates/pack-update.mjs:161`) computes the target and **withholds** it, and the `update` task's apply stage lands it through the member's own PR lane. The cron rewrite reaches every member on the existing nightly cycle with nobody in the loop.

## Phase 1 — the approved stack (one review pass)

All code written before approval is asked for, including the destructive tail.

- [ ] **PR A — #1226 (open).** Design + simulator: `cronHours`, S67–S73, DESIGN §17, coverage rows. Closes #1227.
      *Exit:* merged.
- [ ] **PR B — the vocabulary.** Split `FREQUENCIES` (what a NEW declaration may name) from an accept-at-the-door set, with **one normalization door at declaration load** — not inside `anchorInstant`, because `periodMs` also feeds the janitor's stale-ready bound (`queue/janitor-rules.mjs:103`) and the signal window (`queue/signals.mjs:15`); normalizing only the anchor judges a daily task stale after two hours. Four consumers: `calendar.mjs:25`, `task-contract.mjs:100`, `packs/claudinite-growth/task-declaration-shape.mjs:49` (rejects the retired tokens for new declarations), `slots.mjs:23` (fielded shim, stays).
      Four declarations move: `update` `daily-2h`→`daily`; `growth-extract` `daily-1h`→`daily` (already has `after:`); `fleet-digest` `daily+1h`→`daily` + a new `after:` naming the sheepdog sweeps (safe cross-pack — an undeclared upstream yields no constraint); `usage-fold` `hourly`→`daily` **and its `WINDOW_DAYS = 2/24` must move with it**, or the "session captured" half of its precondition goes permanently dark and a repo whose only movement is commit-less sessions never folds again.
      Plus the cross-repo stagger `after:` cannot express: **set this repo's `taskScheduler.dailyHour` to 5**, so members extract at 04:00 and the canon's `growth-promote` reads their merged mains at 05:00. One line, this repo only, no fleet migration. Add `after: ['claudinite-growth/growth-extract']` to the canon-local `growth-promote` for the within-repo half.
      *Exit:* merged, suite green, S74 (normalized `hourly` behaves as `daily`) added and passing.
- [ ] **PR C — the cron.** `hashedCron` returns two hours derived from `dailyHour`; `converge-wiring.mjs:132` passes the schedule; the vendored stub's placeholder and **the canon's own `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml` change in the same commit** — the canon has no converge, so its copy drifts invisibly otherwise.
      *Exit:* merged; this repo's own workflow reads the two-hour cron.
- [ ] **PR D — the destructive tail, written now, merged later.** Retire the door-normalization and drop the legacy tokens from the accepted set. Body states its merge is gated on Link 3 and names it.
      *Exit:* approved in this pass; **not merged**.

## Phase 2 — the execution chain

Filed as sub-issues of this tracker once the plan is agreed, each naming the previous in `Blocked-by:` so the queue does the waiting.

- [ ] **Link 1 — force delivery and read it back.** Drive Shepherd's `fleet-baseline` with `follow`.
      *Ready when:* PRs B and C are merged.
      *Worked when:* every member's stamp shows the new `packVersions`, **and** its `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml` cron reads `<hashed> H,H+12` for that member's own `dailyHour`. Read per member; a member that cannot be read parks the link open rather than passing — a scope-blocked sweep answers "all clear" exactly like a healthy one.
- [ ] **Link 2 — verify in production.** *Ready when:* Link 1 closed and one full UTC day has passed.
      *Worked when:* each private member's Actions usage shows exactly **2** scheduler runs for that day (baseline: 24), and no task's standing item is missing its occurrence. Also the first read of the risk the sim cannot model — whether a member's whole daily chain now fits one drain against `timeout-minutes: 350`.
- [ ] **Link 3 — retire the tolerance.** *Ready when:* Link 2 closed **and** no member's task declarations still name a retired token — a converge-confirmable precondition, never a calendar date: retiring it while a member still declares `hourly` turns that member's daily task into a two-hour staleness park.
      *Worked when:* PR D merged, suite green.

## Known residual risks

- **Dropped ticks cost 12× more latency** (S71). Nothing is stranded — dueness comes from the anchor, never from whether the cron fired — but a dropped anchor tick now waits until the drain tick. This is why the second tick is not optional.

{"id":5221773732,"number":1225,"state":"open","locked":false,"title":"The hourly scheduler cron is the fleet's whole Actions allowance — move to a twice-daily tick","body":"## The problem

The August usage report puts `claudinite-scheduler.yml` at 1,515 of 2,123 private Actions minutes — **71% of spend** — running at a near-identical ~26 min/day on every private member (MissingBulbWebsite 26.1, WIP 27.0, hitbut 26.0, ClaudiniteWebsite 25.2, EdFringeAllocator 17.0).

Four private members × 24 min/day × 30d = 2,880 min = **$17.28/mo**, which is exactly the $18.00 allowance the report terminates at. The scheduler *is* the allowance, with zero macOS and zero real work. It scales linearly with adoption: WIP and hitbut came online Aug 20–21 and immediately added ~53 min/day between them.

## Why optimising the job buys nothing

Sampled 30 consecutive scheduled runs on this repo: **median 32s wall-clock**, only one over 60s. Actions bills each job rounded up to the whole minute, so ~46% of every billed minute is already rounding waste.

The cost is **run count**, not compute. The only lever is fewer runs.

## What the 24 runs/day are actually buying

Exactly one task in the corpus is `hourly` — `usage-fold` (`packs/claudinite-growth`). Everything else is `daily-2h`/`daily-1h`/`daily`/`daily+1h`/`weekly`/`monthly`/`manual`. Per `engine/scheduler/calendar.mjs`, the whole daily family lands at `dailyHour-2 … dailyHour+1`, with weekly and monthly also at `dailyHour` — so a default member's entire anchor set is four clock hours a day.

Two of the three remaining jobs are already solved elsewhere in the engine:

- **Ordering within a repo.** `after:` shipped (`engine/scheduler/task-contract.mjs:184-192`); `growth-extract` declares it and its own comment says the staggered hours *"express the same intent and cannot enforce it; this can."*
- **Chain continuation.** `executor.mjs:215` re-reads the queue each iteration and calls `readyDependents()` on every close, so a multi-stage chain drains back-to-back in one run.

That leaves adopting newly-marked ad-hoc issues, `Not-before` releases, and dead-claim reclaims as the only work the 23 extra runs a day exist for.

## The end state

`docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` §17, with the measured trade and the rejected alternatives. Cron fires twice daily at `<hashed-minute> <dailyHour>,<(dailyHour+12)%24>`. **24 runs/day → 2**; $17.28/mo → $1.44/mo; a new private member costs 2 min/day instead of 26.

---

# The plan

## Phase 0 — out-of-band setup: **none**

Verified there is no human-only step. No new secret, permission, repo variable or platform setting. The one path a converge cannot push into is `.github/workflows/`, and that is already solved: `pendingSchedulerWorkflow` (`updates/pack-update.mjs:161`) computes the target and **withholds** it, and the `update` task's apply stage lands it through the member's own PR lane. The cron rewrite reaches every member on the existing nightly cycle with nobody in the loop.

## Phase 1 — the approved stack (one review pass)

All code written before approval is asked for, including the destructive tail.

- [ ] **PR A — #1226 (open).** Design + simulator: `cronHours`, S67–S73, DESIGN §17, coverage rows. Closes #1227.
      *Exit:* merged.
- [ ] **PR B — the vocabulary.** Split `FREQUENCIES` (what a NEW declaration may name) from an accept-at-the-door set, with **one normalization door at declaration load** — not inside `anchorInstant`, because `periodMs` also feeds the janitor's stale-ready bound (`queue/janitor-rules.mjs:103`) and the signal window (`queue/signals.mjs:15`); normalizing only the anchor judges a daily task stale after two hours. Four consumers: `calendar.mjs:25`, `task-contract.mjs:100`, `packs/claudinite-growth/task-declaration-shape.mjs:49` (rejects the retired tokens for new declarations), `slots.mjs:23` (fielded shim, stays).
      Four declarations move: `update` `daily-2h`→`daily`; `growth-extract` `daily-1h`→`daily` (already has `after:`); `fleet-digest` `daily+1h`→`daily` + a new `after:` naming the sheepdog sweeps (safe cross-pack — an undeclared upstream yields no constraint); `usage-fold` `hourly`→`daily` **and its `WINDOW_DAYS = 2/24` must move with it**, or the "session captured" half of its precondition goes permanently dark and a repo whose only movement is commit-less sessions never folds again.
      Plus the cross-repo stagger `after:` cannot express: **set this repo's `taskScheduler.dailyHour` to 5**, so members extract at 04:00 and the canon's `growth-promote` reads their merged mains at 05:00. One line, this repo only, no fleet migration. Add `after: ['claudinite-growth/growth-extract']` to the canon-local `growth-promote` for the within-repo half.
      *Exit:* merged, suite green, S74 (normalized `hourly` behaves as `daily`) added and passing.
- [ ] **PR C — the cron.** `hashedCron` returns two hours derived from `dailyHour`; `converge-wiring.mjs:132` passes the schedule; the vendored stub's placeholder and **the canon's own `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml` change in the same commit** — the canon has no converge, so its copy drifts invisibly otherwise.
      *Exit:* merged; this repo's own workflow reads the two-hour cron.
- [ ] **PR D — the destructive tail, written now, merged later.** Retire the door-normalization and drop the legacy tokens from the accepted set. Body states its merge is gated on Link 3 and names it.
      *Exit:* approved in this pass; **not merged**.

## Phase 2 — the execution chain

Filed as sub-issues of this tracker once the plan is agreed, each naming the previous in `Blocked-by:` so the queue does the waiting.

- [ ] **Link 1 — force delivery and read it back.** Drive Shepherd's `fleet-baseline` with `follow`.
      *Ready when:* PRs B and C are merged.
      *Worked when:* every member's stamp shows the new `packVersions`, **and** its `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml` cron reads `<hashed> H,H+12` for that member's own `dailyHour`. Read per member; a member that cannot be read parks the link open rather than passing — a scope-blocked sweep answers "all clear" exactly like a healthy one.
- [ ] **Link 2 — verify in production.** *Ready when:* Link 1 closed and one full UTC day has passed.
      *Worked when:* each private member's Actions usage shows exactly **2** scheduler runs for that day (baseline: 24), and no task's standing item is missing its occurrence. Also the first read of the risk the sim cannot model — whether a member's whole daily chain now fits one drain against `timeout-minutes: 350`.
- [ ] **Link 3 — retire the tolerance.** *Ready when:* Link 2 closed **and** no member's task declarations still name a retired token — a converge-confirmable precondition, never a calendar date: retiring it while a member still declares `hourly` turns that member's daily task into a two-hour staleness park.
      *Worked when:* PR D merged, suite green.

## Known residual risks

- **Dropped ticks cost 12× more latency** (S71). Nothing is stranded — dueness comes from the anchor, never from whether the cron fired — but a dropped anchor tick now waits until the drain tick. This is why the second tick is not optional.
- **Ad-hoc latency goes to a 6h mean / 12h worst case** (S68). An `issues: [labeled]` trigger would take it to seconds for a run only when a mark happens; recorded in §17.5 as additive and deliberately out of this plan's scope.
- **A whole day now settles serially in one Actions job.** The simulator's durations are fixtures, so it cannot say whether a real member's chain fits. Link 2 is the first real measurement.

{"id":5221773732,"number":1225,"state":"open","locked":false,"title":"The hourly scheduler cron is the fleet's whole Actions allowance — move to a twice-daily tick","body":"## The problem

The August usage report puts `claudinite-scheduler.yml` at 1,515 of 2,123 private Actions minutes — **71% of spend** — running at a near-identical ~26 min/day on every private member (MissingBulbWebsite 26.1, WIP 27.0, hitbut 26.0, ClaudiniteWebsite 25.2, EdFringeAllocator 17.0).

Four private members × 24 min/day × 30d = 2,880 min = **$17.28/mo**, which is exactly the $18.00 allowance the report terminates at. The scheduler *is* the allowance, with zero macOS and zero real work. It scales linearly with adoption: WIP and hitbut came online Aug 20–21 and immediately added ~53 min/day between them.

## Why optimising the job buys nothing

Sampled 30 consecutive scheduled runs on this repo: **median 32s wall-clock**, only one over 60s. Actions bills each job rounded up to the whole minute, so ~46% of every billed minute is already rounding waste.

The cost is **run count**, not compute. The only lever is fewer runs.

## What the 24 runs/day are actually buying

Exactly one task in the corpus is `hourly` — `usage-fold` (`packs/claudinite-growth`). Everything else is `daily-2h`/`daily-1h`/`daily`/`daily+1h`/`weekly`/`monthly`/`manual`. Per `engine/scheduler/calendar.mjs`, the whole daily family lands at `dailyHour-2 … dailyHour+1`, with weekly and monthly also at `dailyHour` — so a default member's entire anchor set is four clock hours a day.

Two of the three remaining jobs are already solved elsewhere in the engine:

- **Ordering within a repo.** `after:` shipped (`engine/scheduler/task-contract.mjs:184-192`); `growth-extract` declares it and its own comment says the staggered hours *"express the same intent and cannot enforce it; this can."*
- **Chain continuation.** `executor.mjs:215` re-reads the queue each iteration and calls `readyDependents()` on every close, so a multi-stage chain drains back-to-back in one run.

That leaves adopting newly-marked ad-hoc issues, `Not-before` releases, and dead-claim reclaims as the only work the 23 extra runs a day exist for.

## The end state

`docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` §17, with the measured trade and the rejected alternatives. Cron fires twice daily at `<hashed-minute> <dailyHour>,<(dailyHour+12)%24>`. **24 runs/day → 2**; $17.28/mo → $1.44/mo; a new private member costs 2 min/day instead of 26.

---

# The plan

## Phase 0 — out-of-band setup: **none**

Verified there is no human-only step. No new secret, permission, repo variable or platform setting. The one path a converge cannot push into is `.github/workflows/`, and that is already solved: `pendingSchedulerWorkflow` (`updates/pack-update.mjs:161`) computes the target and **withholds** it, and the `update` task's apply stage lands it through the member's own PR lane. The cron rewrite reaches every member on the existing nightly cycle with nobody in the loop.

## Phase 1 — the approved stack (one review pass)

All code written before approval is asked for, including the destructive tail.

- [ ] **PR A — #1226 (open).** Design + simulator: `cronHours`, S67–S73, DESIGN §17, coverage rows. Closes #1227.
      *Exit:* merged.
- [ ] **PR B — the vocabulary.** Split `FREQUENCIES` (what a NEW declaration may name) from an accept-at-the-door set, with **one normalization door at declaration load** — not inside `anchorInstant`, because `periodMs` also feeds the janitor's stale-ready bound (`queue/janitor-rules.mjs:103`) and the signal window (`queue/signals.mjs:15`); normalizing only the anchor judges a daily task stale after two hours. Four consumers: `calendar.mjs:25`, `task-contract.mjs:100`, `packs/claudinite-growth/task-declaration-shape.mjs:49` (rejects the retired tokens for new declarations), `slots.mjs:23` (fielded shim, stays).
      Four declarations move: `update` `daily-2h`→`daily`; `growth-extract` `daily-1h`→`daily` (already has `after:`); `fleet-digest` `daily+1h`→`daily` + a new `after:` naming the sheepdog sweeps (safe cross-pack — an undeclared upstream yields no constraint); `usage-fold` `hourly`→`daily` **and its `WINDOW_DAYS = 2/24` must move with it**, or the "session captured" half of its precondition goes permanently dark and a repo whose only movement is commit-less sessions never folds again.
      Plus the cross-repo stagger `after:` cannot express: **set this repo's `taskScheduler.dailyHour` to 5**, so members extract at 04:00 and the canon's `growth-promote` reads their merged mains at 05:00. One line, this repo only, no fleet migration. Add `after: ['claudinite-growth/growth-extract']` to the canon-local `growth-promote` for the within-repo half.
      *Exit:* merged, suite green, S74 (normalized `hourly` behaves as `daily`) added and passing.
- [ ] **PR C — the cron.** `hashedCron` returns two hours derived from `dailyHour`; `converge-wiring.mjs:132` passes the schedule; the vendored stub's placeholder and **the canon's own `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml` change in the same commit** — the canon has no converge, so its copy drifts invisibly otherwise.
      *Exit:* merged; this repo's own workflow reads the two-hour cron.
- [ ] **PR D — the destructive tail, written now, merged later.** Retire the door-normalization and drop the legacy tokens from the accepted set. Body states its merge is gated on Link 3 and names it.
      *Exit:* approved in this pass; **not merged**.

## Phase 2 — the execution chain

Filed as sub-issues of this tracker once the plan is agreed, each naming the previous in `Blocked-by:` so the queue does the waiting.

- [ ] **Link 1 — force delivery and read it back.** Drive Shepherd's `fleet-baseline` with `follow`.
      *Ready when:* PRs B and C are merged.
      *Worked when:* every member's stamp shows the new `packVersions`, **and** its `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml` cron reads `<hashed> H,H+12` for that member's own `dailyHour`. Read per member; a member that cannot be read parks the link open rather than passing — a scope-blocked sweep answers "all clear" exactly like a healthy one.
- [ ] **Link 2 — verify in production.** *Ready when:* Link 1 closed and one full UTC day has passed.
      *Worked when:* each private member's Actions usage shows exactly **2** scheduler runs for that day (baseline: 24), and no task's standing item is missing its occurrence. Also the first read of the risk the sim cannot model — whether a member's whole daily chain now fits one drain against `timeout-minutes: 350`.
- [ ] **Link 3 — retire the tolerance.** *Ready when:* Link 2 closed **and** no member's task declarations still name a retired token — a converge-confirmable precondition, never a calendar date: retiring it while a member still declares `hourly` turns that member's daily task into a two-hour staleness park.
      *Worked when:* PR D merged, suite green.

## Known residual risks

- **Dropped ticks cost 12× more latency** (S71). Nothing is stranded — dueness comes from the anchor, never from whether the cron fired — but a dropped anchor tick now waits until the drain tick. This is why the second tick is not optional.
- **Ad-hoc latency goes to a 6h mean / 12h worst case** (S68). An `issues: [labeled]` trigger would take it to seconds for a run only when a mark happens; recorded in §17.5 as additive and deliberately out of this plan's scope.
- **A whole day now settles serially in one Actions job.** The simulator's durations are fixtures, so it cannot say whether a real member's chain fits. Link 2 is the first real measurement.

{"id":5221773732,"number":1225,"state":"open","locked":false,"title":"The hourly scheduler cron is the fleet's whole Actions allowance — move to a twice-daily tick","body":"## The problem

The August usage report puts `claudinite-scheduler.yml` at 1,515 of 2,123 private Actions minutes — **71% of spend** — running at a near-identical ~26 min/day on every private member (MissingBulbWebsite 26.1, WIP 27.0, hitbut 26.0, ClaudiniteWebsite 25.2, EdFringeAllocator 17.0).

Four private members × 24 min/day × 30d = 2,880 min = **$17.28/mo**, which is exactly the $18.00 allowance the report terminates at. The scheduler *is* the allowance, with zero macOS and zero real work. It scales linearly with adoption: WIP and hitbut came online Aug 20–21 and immediately added ~53 min/day between them.

## Why optimising the job buys nothing

Sampled 30 consecutive scheduled runs on this repo: **median 32s wall-clock**, only one over 60s. Actions bills each job rounded up to the whole minute, so ~46% of every billed minute is already rounding waste.

The cost is **run count**, not compute. The only lever is fewer runs.

## What the 24 runs/day are actually buying

Exactly one task in the corpus is `hourly` — `usage-fold` (`packs/claudinite-growth`). Everything else is `daily-2h`/`daily-1h`/`daily`/`daily+1h`/`weekly`/`monthly`/`manual`. Per `engine/scheduler/calendar.mjs`, the whole daily family lands at `dailyHour-2 … dailyHour+1`, with weekly and monthly also at `dailyHour` — so a default member's entire anchor set is four clock hours a day.

Two of the three remaining jobs are already solved elsewhere in the engine:

- **Ordering within a repo.** `after:` shipped (`engine/scheduler/task-contract.mjs:184-192`); `growth-extract` declares it and its own comment says the staggered hours *"express the same intent and cannot enforce it; this can."*
- **Chain continuation.** `executor.mjs:215` re-reads the queue each iteration and calls `readyDependents()` on every close, so a multi-stage chain drains back-to-back in one run.

That leaves adopting newly-marked ad-hoc issues, `Not-before` releases, and dead-claim reclaims as the only work the 23 extra runs a day exist for.

## The end state

`docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` §17, with the measured trade and the rejected alternatives. Cron fires twice daily at `<hashed-minute> <dailyHour>,<(dailyHour+12)%24>`. **24 runs/day → 2**; $17.28/mo → $1.44/mo; a new private member costs 2 min/day instead of 26.

---

# The plan

## Phase 0 — out-of-band setup: **none**

Verified there is no human-only step. No new secret, permission, repo variable or platform setting. The one path a converge cannot push into is `.github/workflows/`, and that is already solved: `pendingSchedulerWorkflow` (`updates/pack-update.mjs:161`) computes the target and **withholds** it, and the `update` task's apply stage lands it through the member's own PR lane. The cron rewrite reaches every member on the existing nightly cycle with nobody in the loop.

## Phase 1 — the approved stack (one review pass)

All code written before approval is asked for, including the destructive tail.

- [ ] **PR A — #1226 (open).** Design + simulator: `cronHours`, S67–S73, DESIGN §17, coverage rows. Closes #1227.
      *Exit:* merged.
- [ ] **PR B — the vocabulary.** Split `FREQUENCIES` (what a NEW declaration may name) from an accept-at-the-door set, with **one normalization door at declaration load** — not inside `anchorInstant`, because `periodMs` also feeds the janitor's stale-ready bound (`queue/janitor-rules.mjs:103`) and the signal window (`queue/signals.mjs:15`); normalizing only the anchor judges a daily task stale after two hours. Four consumers: `calendar.mjs:25`, `task-contract.mjs:100`, `packs/claudinite-growth/task-declaration-shape.mjs:49` (rejects the retired tokens for new declarations), `slots.mjs:23` (fielded shim, stays).
      Four declarations move: `update` `daily-2h`→`daily`; `growth-extract` `daily-1h`→`daily` (already has `after:`); `fleet-digest` `daily+1h`→`daily` + a new `after:` naming the sheepdog sweeps (safe cross-pack — an undeclared upstream yields no constraint); `usage-fold` `hourly`→`daily` **and its `WINDOW_DAYS = 2/24` must move with it**, or the "session captured" half of its precondition goes permanently dark and a repo whose only movement is commit-less sessions never folds again.
      Plus the cross-repo stagger `after:` cannot express: **set this repo's `taskScheduler.dailyHour` to 5**, so members extract at 04:00 and the canon's `growth-promote` reads their merged mains at 05:00. One line, this repo only, no fleet migration. Add `after: ['claudinite-growth/growth-extract']` to the canon-local `growth-promote` for the within-repo half.
      *Exit:* merged, suite green, S74 (normalized `hourly` behaves as `daily`) added and passing.
- [ ] **PR C — the cron.** `hashedCron` returns two hours derived from `dailyHour`; `converge-wiring.mjs:132` passes the schedule; the vendored stub's placeholder and **the canon's own `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml` change in the same commit** — the canon has no converge, so its copy drifts invisibly otherwise.
      *Exit:* merged; this repo's own workflow reads the two-hour cron.
- [ ] **PR D — the destructive tail, written now, merged later.** Retire the door-normalization and drop the legacy tokens from the accepted set. Body states its merge is gated on Link 3 and names it.
      *Exit:* approved in this pass; **not merged**.

## Phase 2 — the execution chain

Filed as sub-issues of this tracker once the plan is agreed, each naming the previous in `Blocked-by:` so the queue does the waiting.

- [ ] **Link 1 — force delivery and read it back.** Drive Shepherd's `fleet-baseline` with `follow`.
      *Ready when:* PRs B and C are merged.
      *Worked when:* every member's stamp shows the new `packVersions`, **and** its `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml` cron reads `<hashed> H,H+12` for that member's own `dailyHour`. Read per member; a member that cannot be read parks the link open rather than passing — a scope-blocked sweep answers "all clear" exactly like a healthy one.
- [ ] **Link 2 — verify in production.** *Ready when:* Link 1 closed and one full UTC day has passed.
      *Worked when:* each private member's Actions usage shows exactly **2** scheduler runs for that day (baseline: 24), and no task's standing item is missing its occurrence. Also the first read of the risk the sim cannot model — whether a member's whole daily chain now fits one drain against `timeout-minutes: 350`.
- [ ] **Link 3 — retire the tolerance.** *Ready when:* Link 2 closed **and** no member's task declarations still name a retired token — a converge-confirmable precondition, never a calendar date: retiring it while a member still declares `hourly` turns that member's daily task into a two-hour staleness park.
      *Worked when:* PR D merged, suite green.

## Known residual risks

- **Dropped ticks cost 12× more latency** (S71). Nothing is stranded — dueness comes from the anchor, never from whether the cron fired — but a dropped anchor tick now waits until the drain tick. This is why the second tick is not optional.
- **Ad-hoc latency goes to a 6h mean / 12h worst case** (S68). An `issues: [labeled]` trigger would take it to seconds for a run only when a mark happens; recorded in §17.5 as additive and deliberately out of this plan's scope.
- **A whole day now settles serially in one Actions job.** The simulator's durations are fixtures, so it cannot say whether a real member's chain fits. Link 2 is the first real measurement.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

## 9. Follow-ups, ordering, fan-in — the dependency fields

`Blocked-by: #N[, #M…]` and `Not-before: <ISO instant>` on an item, evaluated
by the scheduler run (§5). Three patterns fall out, all from the sketch:

- **Follow-up validation.** A task whose run delivered something long-running
  (a store submission, an armed auto-merge, a real-world change that settles
  over days) closes `task:status:done` and creates its own follow-up item:
  `Blocked-by: #<this item>` (satisfied the moment this item closes) +
  `Not-before: <now + settle time>`. The scheduler run readies it when the time passes;
  an executor then re-runs its precondition — which checks whether the world
  actually settled — and the item either runs, or closes obsolete because
  everything landed on its own. The "will anyone check tomorrow?" gap closes
  with machinery that is just two body fields.
- **Ordering, declared — the exclusive claim retires.** A task may declare
  `after: ['basics/baselining']` in `task.mjs`, and it compiles to the
  **pick-time yield** (§6.1), *not* to a `Blocked-by` edge: the executor
  skips the dependent while the upstream's standing item is live
  (ready/executing/agent) this cycle, and picks it the moment the upstream
  converges. The distinction is load-bearing: `Blocked-by` requires the
  blocker *closed*, and a quiet upstream may have no item at all (#1115 — a
  declined anchor files only a board row), so there is nothing for an edge
  to name. (Under the retired roll model the trap was a rolling item that
  never closed, starving every dependent forever — S24's record.) As a
  yield: on the late-fire night all chain items are created together,
  baselining runs first, extract and promote follow *the same night* in
  order; on the routine night where baselining's precondition declines at
  its anchor, no baselining item exists and extract is pickable a minute
  after its own yes. Nothing is spent, no task claims a run, and the engine
  still never knows what baselining is — `after` names a task id, and the
  pick filter reads item states, generically. §12's exclusive-claim
  machinery (and its stated throughput cost) deletes. `Blocked-by` remains
  the right edge for what it is: dependencies on items that *terminate*
  (follow-ups, fan-ins).
- **Fan-out with a fan-in.** Fanning out is creating N items (§8). The fan-in
  is one more item — the status/aggregation task — created `Blocked-by` all N.
  It readies only when every child converged, and its precondition/work step read
  the children's outcome labels to report or escalate. "Getting the status of
  a fan-out" stops being a bespoke sweep and becomes an ordinary task whose
  edges the scheduler run already evaluates.
