content.text:
It's **not** that implementation, and the difference is load-bearing. Here's exactly what it is.

`after:` has two consumers, both the same function — [`executor.mjs:203`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs#L203) (the drain loop's pick) and [`scheduler-run.mjs:787`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/engine/scheduler/queue/scheduler-run.mjs#L787) (the drain gate, calling `pickOrder` only to ask "is anything pickable?"). Plus `conflictsWithEarlierClaim` for race arbitration. **Instantiation never consults it.**

Against your description, clause by clause:

- **"mark that task as blocking me"** — no. Nothing is marked. No `task:blocked` status, no `Blocked-by:` field, no state transition. The item stays `ready` and is simply *skipped this pass*, re-evaluated on every subsequent pass. `Blocked-by:` is the real blocking mechanism and this deliberately isn't it.
- **"an attempt to schedule"** — closer to "an upstream item exists **and** is `ready`/`running-executor`/`running-agent`". An upstream that was asked and **declined** files no item at all (a board row only), so it holds nothing back. Nor does one parked `needs-human` — explicitly so a broken upstream can't halt dependents indefinitely.
- **Missing: standing→standing only.** `if (!standing(i)) return true` — an ad-hoc item ignores `after:` entirely, and a live *ad-hoc* upstream blocks nothing.
- **Missing: same-repo only.** It matches items in this repo's queue, which is exactly what makes `fleet-digest` naming sheepdog tasks safe where that pack isn't declared.

So it's a **soft pick-time yield**, not a block. The drain loop re-reads live each iteration, so the dependent goes the moment the upstream converges — in the same run.

**On `schedule_after`: I'd push back.** Scheduling is precisely the one thing this doesn't touch. The item is instantiated at its own anchor whether or not the upstream is live; only the *pick order* changes. A reader seeing `schedule_after` would reasonably expect the anchor to move — a worse misunderstanding than the one the current name caused.

Worth noting [DESIGN §9](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md) already says this explicitly — *"it compiles to the pick-time yield (§6.1), **not** to a `Blocked-by` edge"*. The doc is right; the field name is what led you elsewhere, which is itself the argument that the name is underselling.

questions.question: Given `after:` is a pick-time yield and not a blocking edge, what should happen to it?

options.label: Rename to yields_to (Recommended)
options.description: The most accurate name for what it does — and it is the word the code and DESIGN §9 already use for the mechanism ("THE `after` YIELD", "yields while that task's item is live"). It carries the softness your reading missed: a yield is voluntary and self-clearing, where `after`/`schedule_after` both read as a hard ordering guarantee. Cost: a task-declaration field is member-owned data no vendoring pass rewrites, so this needs the same door-plus-permanent-tolerance shape I just built for the frequency vocabulary — accept `after` forever, normalize at `normalizeTaskDeclaration`, and let the author-time check reject it for new declarations. Two canon declarations use it today (growth-extract, fleet-digest) plus growth-promote on #1230.

options.label: Keep `after:` as it is
options.description: No rename. DESIGN §9 already states the semantics precisely, the field is only three declarations old, and every rename of a declaration field costs a permanent normalization tolerance in the engine — the corpus now carries one of those for frequencies already. The counter-argument is the one this conversation just demonstrated: the name misled a careful reader who had the design doc available.

options.label: Rename to runs_after
options.description: Keeps the temporal reading you had, which is roughly right, while making it a verb phrase rather than a bare preposition. Cheaper to explain than `yields_to` and reads naturally in a declaration. But it still implies a guarantee the mechanism does not make — a declined or needs-human upstream is skipped entirely, so the dependent can and does run without its named upstream having run at all.

options.label: Change the implementation to real blocking
options.description: Make it mean what you described: mark the dependent `task:blocked` with a `Blocked-by:` edge while the upstream is live. I'd advise against — `Blocked-by` releases on the blocker CLOSING, and a quiet upstream often has no item to name (a declined anchor files only a board row), so there would be nothing for the edge to point at. It also reintroduces the stuck-blocked failure the janitor has a dedicated rule for, and the starvation trap S24 records from the retired roll model. Choose this only if you want ordering to be a hard guarantee and accept dependents wedging when an upstream breaks.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

Popup dismissed — nothing changed. Here's the answer to what you actually asked.

## No, that's not the implementation

`after:` has exactly two consumers, and both are the same function — `pickOrder` in [`engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs:67`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs#L67), called from the executor's drain at `:203` and from the scheduler's *drain gate* at [`scheduler-run.mjs:787`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/engine/scheduler/queue/scheduler-run.mjs#L787), where it only asks "is anything pickable?". Plus `conflictsWithEarlierClaim` at `:128` for the two-executor race.

The filter is three lines:

```js
const live = (item) => [READY, RUNNING_EXECUTOR, RUNNING_AGENT].some((s) => isStatus(item, s));
const liveUpstream = (id) => open.some((o) => idOf(o) === id && standing(o) && live(o));
.filter((i) => standing(i) ? !taskAfter(idOf(i)).some(liveUpstream) : true)
```

Four ways your reading differs, in order of how much they matter:

1. **Nothing is marked.** No `task:blocked`, no `Blocked-by:`, no state transition. The item stays `ready` and is simply skipped by this pass. It's a filter, re-evaluated on every pick — the drain loop re-reads live each iteration, so the dependent becomes pickable the moment the upstream closes, inside the same run. `Blocked-by:` is the repo's real blocking edge, and this deliberately isn't it.

2. **Instantiation never consults it.** Nothing in job 1 reads `after:`. The occurrence is created at its own anchor regardless of what any upstream is doing.

3. **Standing→standing only.** `if (!standing(i)) return true` — an ad-hoc item ignores `after:` entirely, and a live *ad-hoc* upstream holds nothing back.

4. **A missing upstream is no constraint.** A declined upstream files no item at all (only a board row), and one parked `needs-human` isn't `live` — both deliberate, so a broken upstream can't wedge its dependents forever. Same-repo only, which is what makes `fleet-digest` naming sheepdog tasks safe where that pack isn't declared.

So: your condition "if it is that implementation" isn't met, and I haven't renamed anything.

## And `schedule_after` would be the wrong name regardless

Scheduling is the one thing `after:` doesn't touch — point 2 above. A reader seeing `schedule_after` would expect the anchor to move, which is a worse misunderstanding than the one the current name caused.

That said, your misreading is real evidence the name underperforms, and you had the design doc available. If it should change, the accurate word is **`yields_to`** — which is what the code and [DESIGN §9](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md) already call it in prose ("THE `after` YIELD", "it compiles to the **pick-time yield** … *not* to a `Blocked-by` edge"). A yield reads as voluntary and self-clearing; `after` and `schedule_after` both read as a guarantee the mechanism doesn't make.

The cost is not trivial: a task-declaration field is member-owned data no vendoring pass rewrites, so a rename needs the same permanent door-and-tolerance shape I built for the frequency vocabulary in [#1230](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1230) — accept `after` forever, normalize at `normalizeTaskDeclaration`, reject it at author time. Three declarations use it: `growth-extract`, plus `fleet-digest` and `growth-promote` on that branch.

I'd also change your third option: making it a real `Blocked-by` edge reintroduces the starvation trap S24 records from the retired roll model, because a quiet upstream often has no item for an edge to name.

You're right on both counts, and I was wrong on both.

input.body:
Phases B and C of #1225, together — they have to land in the same cycle. A member with the collapsed vocabulary but the old cron keeps paying for 24 ticks; one with the new cron but the old vocabulary fires its `daily±Nh` tasks at hours no tick lands on.

Design: `docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` §17, merged in #1226.

## B — the vocabulary

`FREQUENCIES` becomes `daily`/`weekly`/`monthly`/`manual`. `hourly` cannot mean anything under a cron that fires twice a day, and the `daily±Nh` offsets staggered dependent tasks by clock hour where the ordering field declares the same intent and actually enforces it.

**The door is at declaration load** (`normalizeTaskDeclaration`), not in the calendar. A frequency is read by more than the anchor — `periodMs` feeds the janitor's stale-ready bound and the precondition's signal window — so normalizing only `anchorInstant` would judge a task that now runs daily **stale after two hours**, parking it `needs-human` on exactly the members the tolerance exists to protect.

Four declarations move. `usage-fold`'s carries the trap — its `WINDOW_DAYS` was sized to its hourly period, and left there the "session captured" arm never fires again.

The cross-repo ordering the field **cannot** express — members extract, then this repo's `growth-promote` reads what merged on their mains — moves to this repo's own `dailyHour`, now 5 against members' default 4.

## C — the cron

`hashedCron` returns `<minute> <dailyHour>,<(dailyHour+12)%24> * * *`, threaded through `convergeWiring`, the pack-update lane and bootstrap. Pinning the hours to a constant would fire every task before its anchor on any member that moved its schedule — a day late forever, with nothing going red — so the rehearsal gains a `custom-anchor-hour` shape and `converge-wiring` asserts the hours that actually land.

`scheduler-workflow-shape` accepts both cron forms: `.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot push, so a member holds its hourly cron until its apply-stage PR lands.

## `after:` → `schedule_after:` (added after review)

The bare preposition invited reading the field as a time. It isn't one — its value is a list of `<pack>/<task>` ids, and what it steers is when the item is **scheduled onto an executor**: `pickOrder` is a scheduler in the dispatch sense, and this field is how a task says "not while those are live".

`LEGACY_FIELDS` already carried this exact shape for `agent_preprocessing` → `code_work`, so `after` normalizes at the door permanently and draws an advisory rename — a member's own task file keeps its ordering rather than silently losing it, and its CI doesn't go red over a file nobody has edited.

Two bugs this turned up and fixed:

- The repo-wide sweep rewrote the new finding's own remedy into *"rename schedule_after to schedule_after"*. Its regex is now anchored on a non-word character so it can't match the canonical spelling's tail, with a test pinning that.
- The sweep renamed the simulator's cast declarations and left `registry.get(…)?.after` behind — silently dropping every yield. Three scenarios caught it.

## Consumer safety

Chose the **fixture**, not a migration record: nothing here renames or requires anything of a member's own files — both retired vocabularies are accepted forever at the door. `custom-anchor-hour` is the new shape.

## See-it-fail

Each guard driven red and back: the frequency door (2 engine tests), the author-time frequency strictness, the drifted default hour, the canon's cron against the computed value, the converge ignoring `dailyHour`, the `cronHours` filter (all seven cadence scenarios), the `after` door, and the advisory.

Suite 2608/2608. `check_the_work` and `check_the_world` both 0 blocking.

Closes #1231

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.
